question: Under the Code of Conduct for the Members of the European Commission, for Members to accept free travel offered by third parties, they must either obtain prior approval of the President of the Commission or the travel must be in accordance with diplomatic usage. 1.
Which Members of the Commission have accepted free travel from third parties in the current legislative term?
What specific trips did this involve in each case (including date, destination, travel purpose, identity of the third-party inviter)?
The Commission is requested to provide a corresponding overview for the years 2024 and 2025, following the same approach as in the answer to question for written answer E000189/251.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.5.2026) The Commission would like to refer the Honourable Member to the information on missions expenses and third parties, which was provided in the answer to written question E-000189/251.

Information on missions by the Members of the Commission for the year 2025 and subsequent years is or will be made publicly available on dedicated webpages which ensure transparency of missions for the public2 for both the President and the Members of the Commission. This information also details the cost breakdown of mission elements – such as travel, accommodation, daily allowances, and miscellaneous expenses.
The reason and cost of each mission is systematically published once the billing process is concluded.
